cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

mechanism: A corrects the customer-service smile it taught its now-boss pupil, asking that person to let distress be visible to A.
confusable: Not rejecting professional competence: A limits the old performance to customers and offers private honest company.
comparison: Former trainee employer versus lonely host.
